text:
The Gulf states and Turkey are reportedly urging Trump not to restart large scale strikes on Iran, the Financial Times reports.

They are pushing for a negotiated way out instead, building on talks like today's meeting with Qatar.

🚨 Follow up: A Utah judge has set June 21, 2028 for jury selection in the trial of Tyler Robinson, accused of assassinating Charlie Kirk.

Judge Tony Graf has reserved 105 court days for the case and ordered monthly pretrial conferences.

Follow up: A US Air Force Gulfstream C 37A VIP jet, callsign SPAR84, has also flown in from Ramstein Air Base as the Russian Tu 154M heads from Tel Aviv to Abu Dhabi.

All eyes are on the Abu Dhabi talks on the Russia Ukraine war.
Follow up: Pete Hegseth will hold a rare press conference on Tuesday morning to respond to the impeachment push, as the House heads toward a vote.
CNN projects Democrat Eileen Laubacher will unseat Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's congressional race.

Pakistan: Tehrik e Taliban Pakistan (TTP) militants have blocked highways and set up checkpoints in the Makran region.

One of their trucks carries a Russian made NSV 12.7 "Utyos" heavy machine gun, a rare sight among the group's weapons.
🚨 The Supreme Court has cleared the way for the Trump administration to keep building the southern border wall in Texas, including stretches inside Big Bend National Park.

Follow up: The Russian government Tu 154M (RA 85042) has left Tel Aviv after a 24 hour stay and landed in Abu Dhabi.

Steve Witkoff's jet (N103WG) also touched down in Abu Dhabi earlier today, ahead of the Russia Ukraine talks set for November 10 and 11.

Trump says Qatar and Saudi Arabia would rather see a peaceful end to the conflict with Iran.

But he warns the United States is still ready to launch strikes if it has to.

Follow up: Talks between Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Qatar's prime minister at the White House were described as "positive", Axios reports.

The discussions focused on moving negotiations with Iran forward.

🚨 Al Arabiya reports details of a proposed US nuclear deal with Iran.

Washington would allow Iran to enrich uranium up to 3.67%, which Tehran has reportedly accepted. Iran would cut its stockpile of 60% enriched uranium, and IAEA inspectors would return.
European leaders reportedly held a phone call with Putin earlier this month to gauge his state of mind, and came away convinced he is not ready for negotiations, POLITICO reports.

OPEC oil output rose in October to about 90% of its pre war rate, a Reuters survey shows, led by gains in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq.

Exports are still held back by the Iran war and the US blockade on Iranian shipments.

Marco Rubio says Israel has "clearly graduated" beyond US military financing.

He says Israel is now rich enough to buy American weapons on its own, without the US having to fund the purchases.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the ICC: "Today it's Netanyahu; tomorrow it could be an American."

He says the issue is the court claiming jurisdiction over countries that never joined the treaty: "We didn't join. We're not a member."

Follow up: Rep. Thomas Massie has introduced articles of impeachment against War Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Rubio is backing him: "I think he's done a great job. He's very smart. He works very hard."

Hegseth says he is ready to defend his record.

Yemeni government forces say they have seized Houthi positions on the al Muhawala front in western Lahj after a large assault, claiming dozens of Houthi fighters were killed or wounded.

The Houthis keep firing missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.
Follow up: New satellite imagery reveals the aftermath of the strike on the radar and wireless communications site on Didamar Island, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz.

Houthi fighters have released footage of sniper attacks on the Taiz front in Yemen.

They appear to use several marksman and sniper rifles, possibly including 12.7mm AM 50 "Khatef" anti materiel rifles firing tracer rounds.

Follow up: France vows to push for European sanctions on Iran after blaming Tehran for last month's cyberattack that heated up fridges and freezers in hundreds of French supermarkets.

Paris has also summoned Iran's ambassador.
